purpose: Add eight source-exact public-domain quotations for Bible study and preaching preparation through a duplicate-safe batch importer.

defaults.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the excerpt is verified against the stored text.

entries.title: Read and take God at His word
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: I cannot read other minds and other hearts; I cannot read the Bible and lay hold for others; but I can read for myself, and take God at his word.
entries.slideText: I can read for myself, and take God at his word.
entries.sourceLocator: Assurance, paragraph beginning 'One thing I know'
entries.recommendedUse: Use in a lesson on personally hearing, believing, and receiving the Word of God.
entries.reviewNote: Moody's personal application should be read alongside the cited KJV passages and their contexts.

entries.title: Assurance in the Word
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: There is no doubt about assurance in the Word of God.
entries.slideText: There is no doubt about assurance in the Word of God.
entries.recommendedUse: Use to introduce a Scripture-led study of biblical assurance.
entries.reviewNote: The quotation is a summary claim; establish the doctrine from the cited KJV passages rather than from the quotation alone.

entries.title: Give a reason for the faith
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: I like a man to be able to give a reason for the faith that is in him.
entries.slideText: I like a man to be able to give a reason for the faith that is in him.
entries.sourceLocator: Belief, paragraph beginning 'I like a man'
entries.recommendedUse: Use in teaching believers to know why they believe and to answer with meekness and fear.
entries.reviewNote: Pair the saying with the full wording and context of 1 Peter 3:15 KJV.

entries.title: Cling close to the Bible
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: Oh, let us cling close to the Bible.
entries.slideText: Oh, let us cling close to the Bible.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as a brief exhortation before Bible reading or at the close of a lesson.
entries.reviewNote: The exhortation is concise; the cited KJV passages supply its biblical basis.

entries.title: The depth of God's Book
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: If everybody could understand everything the Bible said it wouldn't be God's book; if Christians, if theologians, had studied it for forty, fifty, sixty years, and then only began to understand it, how could a man expect to understand it by one reading?
entries.slideText: how could a man expect to understand it by one reading?
entries.recommendedUse: Use to encourage repeated, prayerful study rather than hasty conclusions.
entries.reviewNote: Difficulty alone does not prove divine origin; use the quotation as encouragement, not as an argument replacing Scripture.

entries.title: Faith and possibility
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: My friends, if you have faith all things are possible.
entries.slideText: My friends, if you have faith all things are possible.
entries.sourceLocator: Faith, 'How Moody's Faith Saved an Infidel'
entries.recommendedUse: Use only while carefully explaining biblical faith and the will of God from the cited passages.
entries.reviewNote: Do not use this as a promise that every personal desire will occur; read the saying within Moody's evangelistic context and Scripture's teaching.

entries.title: Pillars and windows of a sermon
entries.author: Thomas Fuller, quoted by C. H. Spurgeon
entries.text: Reasons are the pillars of the fabric of a sermon; but similitudes are the windows which give the best lights.
entries.slideText: Reasons are the pillars of the fabric of a sermon; but similitudes are the windows which give the best lights.
entries.recommendedUse: Use in preacher training to distinguish a sermon's reasoning from its illuminating comparisons.
entries.reviewNote: This is Fuller's metaphor as quoted by Spurgeon; Scripture governs both sermon substance and method.

entries.title: Learning expressed plainly
entries.author: Joshua Shute, quoted by C. H. Spurgeon
entries.text: That sermon has most learning in it that has most plainness.
entries.slideText: That sermon has most learning in it that has most plainness.
entries.sourceLocator: Illustrations in Preaching, paragraph discussing obscure sermons
entries.recommendedUse: Use in teaching preachers to make biblical truth understandable rather than obscure.
entries.reviewNote: Plainness must remain accurate and reverent; it is not permission to flatten difficult doctrines.
